provenance.excerpt: excluding (and excluding the effect of), without duplication, (2) ... (19)
excluding (and excluding the effect of), without duplication, (2) ... (19) ... In addition ... Consolidated Net Income will include ...

sufficiencyReasons: Core additive/subtractive structure of all enumerated exclusion clauses (2,4-17,19; clauses 1,3,20 reserved) and the trailing addition paragraph is fully represented with citations and, where the text itself sets a numeric proviso (clause 11's $5,000,000 aggregate cap on unsuccessful-transaction costs), that cap is modeled explicitly.

Two open-ended cross-references ('permitted under this Agreement' in clause (13); 'permitted hereunder' in the trailing addition paragraph) point to unspecified other provisions governing permitted dispositions and cannot be resolved to a specific section from this text; the underlying dollar metrics are still represented, but the referenced scope is dispositioned AMBIGUOUS rather than resolved.

Clause (6)'s waiver carve-out turns on a subjective 'reasonably believes ... using commercially reasonable efforts' standard that is inherently qualitative; it is preserved descriptively within the excluded-Net-Income metric's scope (see irExtensionCandidates) rather than modeled as a separate boolean gate, since no existing IR primitive represents a non-numeric legal eligibility standard.

provenance.excerpt: "Consolidated Net Income" means, with respect to any Person for any period, the net income (loss) of such Person and its Subsidiaries for such period determined on a consolidated basis in accordance with GAAP, excluding (and excluding the effect of), without duplication, ...

irExtensionCandidates.sourceEvidence: §1.01(6): 'unless such restriction ... has been legally waived (or the Borrower reasonably believes such restriction could be waived and is using commercially reasonable efforts to pursue such waiver)'
irExtensionCandidates.semanticRequirement: A gating eligibility test based on a subjective, non-numeric legal/factual standard (existence of an unwaived contractual/statutory/regulatory dividend restriction, or a good-faith 'reasonably believes ... using commercially reasonable efforts' cure-in-progress standard) that determines whether an exclusion applies, with no comparable metric value to run through COMPARE.
irExtensionCandidates.whyExistingPrimitivesFail: COMPARE requires two same-typed quantifiable values; IF's condition slot has no primitive for a qualitative/legal-standard boolean not derived from a metric, transaction input, or numeric comparison - forcing either a fabricated BOOLEAN_LITERAL (misrepresenting a contested/undetermined fact as fixed) or an UNSUPPORTED placeholder that would discard the real eligibility logic rather than just flagging its qualitative nature.
irExtensionCandidates.candidateGeneralizedPrimitive: QUALITATIVE_LEGAL_GATE(description, standardType) - a first-class boolean-valued node representing a qualitative/legal eligibility standard (e.g. 'WAIVED_OR_REASONABLE_EFFORTS_CURE', 'GOVERNMENTAL_APPROVAL_OBTAINED'), usable wherever a COMPARE/IF condition is expected, without asserting a specific truth value.

Two open-ended cross-references ('permitted under this Agreement' in clause (13); 'permitted hereunder' in the trailing addition paragraph) point to unspecified other provisions governing permitted dispositions and cannot be resolved to a specific section from this text; the underlying dollar metrics are still represented, but the referenced scope is dispositioned AMBIGUOUS rather than resolved.

Clause (6)'s waiver carve-out turns on a subjective 'reasonably believes ... using commercially reasonable efforts' standard that is inherently qualitative; it is preserved descriptively within the excluded-Net-Income metric's scope (see irExtensionCandidates) rather than modeled as a separate boolean gate, since no existing IR primitive represents a non-numeric legal eligibility standard.

irExtensionCandidates.sourceEvidence: §1.01(6): 'unless such restriction ... has been legally waived (or the Borrower reasonably believes such restriction could be waived and is using commercially reasonable efforts to pursue such waiver)'
irExtensionCandidates.semanticRequirement: A gating eligibility test based on a subjective, non-numeric legal/factual standard (existence of an unwaived contractual/statutory/regulatory dividend restriction, or a good-faith 'reasonably believes ... using commercially reasonable efforts' cure-in-progress standard) that determines whether an exclusion applies, with no comparable metric value to run through COMPARE.
irExtensionCandidates.whyExistingPrimitivesFail: COMPARE requires two same-typed quantifiable values; IF's condition slot has no primitive for a qualitative/legal-standard boolean not derived from a metric, transaction input, or numeric comparison - forcing either a fabricated BOOLEAN_LITERAL (misrepresenting a contested/undetermined fact as fixed) or an UNSUPPORTED placeholder that would discard the real eligibility logic rather than just flagging its qualitative nature.
irExtensionCandidates.candidateGeneralizedPrimitive: QUALITATIVE_LEGAL_GATE(description, standardType) - a first-class boolean-valued node representing a qualitative/legal eligibility standard (e.g. 'WAIVED_OR_REASONABLE_EFFORTS_CURE', 'GOVERNMENTAL_APPROVAL_OBTAINED'), usable wherever a COMPARE/IF condition is expected, without asserting a specific truth value.

findings.sourceEvidence: In addition, to the extent not already included in the Consolidated Net Income of such Person and its Subsidiaries, Consolidated Net Income will include the amount of proceeds received or receivable from business interruption insurance, the amount of any expenses or charges incurred by such Person or its Subsidiaries during such period that are, directly or indirectly, reimbursed or reimbursable by a third party, and amounts that are covered by indemnification or other reimbursement provisions in connection with any acquisition, Investment or any sale, conveyance, transfer or other disposition of assets permitted hereunder.
findings.proposedIrEvidence: The 'additions' bucket (business interruption insurance proceeds, third-party reimbursed/reimbursable expenses, indemnification/reimbursement amounts) is modeled as an unconditional SUM added to Net Income (ir-expr:7f1643d1dbaddd504d93856c), even though the compiler's own quoted excerpt in that node's provenance includes the gating phrase 'to the extent not already included in the Consolidated Net Income'.
findings.verifierReasoning: The source expressly conditions these three add-back items on their not already being reflected in the base Net Income figure - this is an anti-double-counting proviso, not merely descriptive language. The proposed IR sums these amounts onto Net Income with no deduction/dedup logic, so if the referenced metrics (e.g., business interruption insurance proceeds, which are typically already recognized as GAAP income) are already embedded in the base 'Net Income (GAAP, consolidated basis)' metric, the formula as modeled would double-count them, systematically overstating Consolidated Net Income. Because Consolidated Net Income is a foundational building block for EBITDA, leverage ratios, and Restricted Payment/Investment capacity throughout the credit agreement, an inflated CNI could materially misstate available covenant capacity. This is an independently operative proviso in the source that the proposed IR (marked only generically 'PARTIAL') does not specifically encode.

findings.sourceEvidence: the Net Income for such period of any Subsidiary (other than any Guarantor) to the extent that the declaration or payment of dividends or similar distributions by that any Subsidiary of its Net Income is not at the date of determination permitted without any prior governmental approval (which has not been obtained) or, directly or indirectly, by the operation of the terms of its charter or any agreement, instrument, judgment, decree, order, statute, rule or governmental regulation applicable to that Subsidiary or its stockholders, unless such restriction with respect to the payment of dividends or similar distributions has been legally waived (or the Borrower reasonably believes such restriction could be waived and is using commercially reasonable efforts to pursue such waiver)
findings.proposedIrEvidence: The exclusion is represented as a METRIC_REFERENCE named 'Net Income of a Subsidiary (other than a Guarantor) subject to an unwaived dividend/distribution restriction' inside a SUBTRACT node, with no explicit boolean/condition node encoding the 'unless legally waived' carve-out or the 'Borrower reasonably believes such restriction could be waived and is using commercially reasonable efforts to pursue such waiver' alternative safe harbor.
findings.verifierReasoning: Clause (6)'s exclusion is entirely gated on a multi-part legal/factual condition (no governmental approval obtained AND contractual/charter restriction in effect, UNLESS legally waived or reasonably believed waivable with commercially reasonable efforts being pursued). The proposed IR folds this entire condition into the label of a single metric reference rather than modeling it as explicit conditional logic, so a downstream consumer resolving this metric has no structured guidance on how the waiver/reasonable-efforts prong should be evaluated - only a prose hint in the metric name. Because the metric name does at least gesture at 'unwaived,' this is a partial capture rather than a full omission, and the definition is already marked 'PARTIAL,' so materiality is uncertain rather than clearly established; but a reviewer relying on the IR's structure alone could miss that the waiver/reasonable-efforts safe harbor is a real, separately operative override of the exclusion.
